title: Mosaic Pool Microdashboard — Burst & Health Controls Prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Design a compact, single-pane microdashboard for dedicated GPU pools (internal codename: Mosaic) that surfaces health, cost implications, and fast autoscale/burst controls for on-call operators and platform engineers. This ticket covers the mid-fidelity prototype, rationale for control affordances, and handoff artifacts for PM/Eng review.

Key goals:
- Make burst activation and scheduled bursts discoverable and reversible in <3 clicks.
- Surface thermal/slot saturation and tail-latency risks alongside immediate cost delta when toggling burst.
- Provide a predictive preview that estimates expected latency/throughput change and estimated incremental cost for the next 15/60/240 minutes.
- Ensure safe defaults and a budget guardrail with an explicit confirm for high-cost bursts.
- Fit into existing console list/detail flow as an optional collapsible rail or a floating micro panel for mobile/responsive screens.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Prototype screens in Figma with annotated states: idle, low-traffic, saturating, emergency-burst, scheduled-burst.
2) Interaction flows for: quick-burst (instant), scheduled-burst, cancel-scheduled, and emergency-fallback.
3) A concise 'predictive preview' widget that shows latency pct change and cost delta for 15/60/240 minute horizons.
4) PM and Eng have reviewed and left actionable comments in the Figma file.
5) Handoff checklist completed (tokens: CSS vars, spacing, design tokens) and PRD link included.
6) Accessibility checks documented (contrast, keyboard focus, screen reader labels).
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff with PM and runtime lead (notes: show both per-pool and per-model partition toggles; runtime asked for sample telemetry endpoints).
2026-02-13: Low-fi sketches validated with oncall engineer; changed placement of 'budget guardrail' from modal to inline banner when predicted cost > 8% of daily reserved spend.
2026-02-15: Mid-fi prototype created in Figma: microdashboard includes SLO ribbon, thermal band, slot-util histogram, burst knob, schedule mini-cal, and predictive preview card.

2026-02-16: Design review with PM and two backend engineers: asked for explicit API contract fields (burst_duration, target_slots, force_override, reason_tag). Added small 'reason' text field to quick-burst flow for audit logs.
2026-02-18: Incorporated review feedback: added an option to 'preview with KV-cache warm' to show optimistic latency improvements; flagged a security review if audit log retention < 90 days.
2026-02-18: Submitted prototype for stakeholder review (link in Links).
comments: PM - Jordan Kim (2026-02-15): Love the predictive preview. Please ensure cost estimate includes reserved vs burst billing buckets. Also add a 'why this matters' tooltip for non-platform engineers.

Eng - Priya Nair (2026-02-16): Need to confirm available telemetry: tail latency p99/995, slot utilization, GPU temperature, and active KV-cache hit rate. Will follow up with an example JSON payload from the runtime team.
Oncall - Marco Santos (2026-02-17): Prefer quick-burst confirmation to include estimated SLA risk percentage; update mock to show historical outage events filtered to pool.
decisions: Inline budget guardrail instead of modal confirmation when predicted cost increase < 5% of daily commit.
Require a short-text 'reason' for emergency-burst to populate audit logs (max 120 chars).
Expose 'KV-cache warm' toggle in preview only; not default to avoid misleading optimistic estimates.
next_steps: Address Eng's telemetry contract: add example telemetry mapping to the handoff checklist (due 2026-02-20).
Run 5 moderated usability sessions with SRE/on-call participants (targets: time-to-burst, comprehension of cost delta).
Update prototype with localization-ready labels and run accessibility audit (contrast, keyboard order).
Create a lightweight PRD for behavior when burst requests are denied by capacity policy (edge cases).
Handoff to frontend with storybook tokens and micro-interaction specs.
